condition: Since v1.11.10, dayjs.duration(ms) built from a diff spanning a month or more splits the milliseconds into months/days/hours using fractional average month/year lengths, so days() and hours() come out wrong (e.g. 11 instead of 23 hours).
workaround: Don't break a millisecond duration into calendar parts. Use date2.diff(date1, 'month'), 'day' and 'hour' and work out the remainders yourself, or stay on dayjs 1.11.9.
